content.text:
Self-dev mode is jcode's mechanism for modifying its own source code. Here's how it works and how it's meant to be used:

## How to use it

1. **Clone the jcode repo** (<https://github.com/1jehuang/jcode>) and run `jcode` from inside it. When running `jcode` inside the jcode repository, it auto-detects the repo and enables self-dev mode. There's no flag to pass, the detection is automatic.
2. **Just tell the agent what to change.** Tell your jcode agent to enter self dev mode, and it will start modifying its own source code. Jcode is optimized to iterate on itself.

## What happens under the hood

When a session starts in the jcode repo, it connects to the normal shared jcode server, marks that session as canary/self-dev via subscribe metadata, enables selfdev prompt/tooling only for that session, and `/reload` still hot-reloads the shared server so clients reconnect.

The reload flow: the client sends a Reload request, the server execs into the new binary with serve args, the new server process starts on the same socket, all clients auto-reconnect, and the initiating client also re-execs if its binary is outdated.

## Intended usage pattern

The design intent is full-loop autonomy: there is significant infrastructure around self development, which allows it to edit, build, and test its own source code, then reload its own binary and continue work in your (potentially many) sessions, fully automatically.

Two practices the docs emphasize:

- **Verify at runtime, not just at build time.** A successful build alone is not runtime validation. When testing a rebuilt server, use an isolated socket or the coordinated self-dev reload path so the long-lived daemon is actually running the changed binary.
- **Don't disrupt an in-use daemon.** For safe verification, build with the selfdev profile and run the resulting binary against its own socket rather than restarting an in-use shared daemon; a production activation must use the established safe build/reload workflow. You can isolate with `jcode --socket /tmp/test.sock` style launches so your other sessions keep running on the stable binary.

**TL;DR:** `cd` into a jcode checkout, launch `jcode`, and ask it to make the change you want. It edits, builds, tests, then `/reload`s the shared server in place while your sessions reconnect automatically.
